title: A recursive call jumps back to the start
statement: A recursive call is a jump back to the beginning of the function, using the same variables, so there is only ever one copy of the function running.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: trace a recursive function that does work after the recursive call
evidence_patterns.signature: omits or misorders the work done after each call returns

discriminators.vs_slip: Consistent across items with post-call work; the learner draws a single frame. A slip is a single ordering error.

vs.prog.func.base-case-not-needed: Base-case omitters are diagnosed by termination questions; loop-model holders by post-call ordering.

conflicts_with.label: Each recursive call has its own activation with its own variables

resolved_by.label: Each recursive call has its own activation with its own variables

sources.citation: Kahney, H. (1983). What do novice programmers know about recursion? In Proceedings of the SIGCHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '83), 235-239.
Götschi, T., Sanders, I., & Galpin, V. (2003). Mental models of recursion. In Proceedings of the 34th SIGCSE Technical Symposium on Computer Science Education (SIGCSE '03), 346-350.
sources.note: Mental models of recursion including looping and active/passive-flow models.
